title: proxy_alerts plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `proxy_alerts` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component ProxyAlertsConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

DisconnectCause.description: Stream session termination cause. `gateway_policy` is a gateway admission or dispatch-policy decision before any backend was selected (for example opaque-TLS SNI fail-closed refusal).

ErrorClass.description:
Stable classification of a backend dispatch failure. Emitted on
`TransactionSummary.error_class` / `StreamTransactionSummary.error_class`
and used by alert rules. `graceful_remote_close` is the HTTP/3 backend's
spec-legal teardown signal (RFC 9114 §8.1) — the request still 502s but
the connection stays H3-capable. `dispatch_policy_rejected` covers
terminal gateway decisions taken before any backend dial (for example
an unsupportable backend TLS SNI override) and is intentionally not a
connection error, so retry policies do not fire.
`gateway_buffer_capacity` is the gateway's process-wide budget for
*retained* (buffered) response bodies refusing another response: the
backend answered correctly and within every configured per-response
ceiling, so the refusal is gateway-local transient capacity. It is
health-neutral (no circuit-breaker, passive-health, or
adaptive-concurrency effect) and not retried, and it surfaces as HTTP
`503` or gRPC `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` — never as a backend `502` /
`response_body_too_large`.
`backend_connection_limit` is the gateway refusing to open one more
physical backend connection because the destination is already at its
DestinationRule `connectionPool.tcp.maxConnections` ceiling. Nothing was
dialed, so it is health-neutral (no circuit-breaker, passive-health,
load-balancer-penalty, or adaptive-concurrency effect) — a saturated
operator-configured ceiling must never eject a healthy destination —
while still being pre-wire, so `retry_on_connect_failure` may rotate to
another load-balanced target with its own admission lane.
`trust_withdrawn` is a gateway-to-mesh transport refused because an
accepted gateway trust publication withdrew an authority: the connection
was dialed under the outgoing trust generation, or a checked-out
transport was retired before it could open the next stream. Nothing was
sent, so it is health-neutral for the same reason as
`backend_connection_limit` — withdrawing a root is gateway policy, not
evidence about the destination workload — while staying pre-wire, so a
retry re-dials under the freshly published trust generation.

ProxyAlertsConfig.description:
Plugin: proxy_alerts — in-gateway anomaly notifications for proxy
traffic. Observes HTTP/gRPC transaction summaries, TCP/UDP stream
disconnect summaries, and WebSocket disconnect summaries, then sends
Trigger/Resolve notifications to Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord,
generic HTTP webhooks, or SMTP email. See docs/proxy_alerts.md.

Unknown top-level keys are rejected. Present values must match their
declared types (`enabled` boolean, `quiet_hours_utc` array,
`max_concurrent_dispatches` integer 1..=4294967295, `max_delivery_retries`
integer 0..=8, `delivery_retry_base_ms` / `delivery_retry_max_ms`
integers in [10, 60000]). The constructor additionally requires
`delivery_retry_max_ms >= delivery_retry_base_ms`; standard JSON Schema
cannot compare those sibling numbers, so this schema does not claim
complete admission equivalence for that pair. The `channels` map remains
open for arbitrary channel names; each channel/rule variant is closed
to its selected shape. Rules may also be `enabled: false` drafts.
Webhook `method` is case-insensitive (constructor normalizes to
POST / PUT / PATCH). Channel URL and `*_env` strings must be nonempty;
HTTP webhook URLs must be HTTP(S) with a host and no userinfo.

Email `subject_template` / `body_template` reject empty strings.
Schema `maxLength` on those fields is a character ceiling for tooling;
the constructor enforces UTF-8 byte bounds (1024 / 65536) and balanced
`${` template syntax. SMTP `username` / `username_env` must be paired
with `password` / `password_env` and vice versa. `from` / `to` use the
constructor's ASCII addr-spec grammar (not annotation-only `format: email`).

Registration is OptionalFailOpen. Admin create/update performs strict
construction and returns HTTP 400 for an invalid enabled config before
storing it. During file-mode load, `ferrum-edge validate`, pre-existing
DB/CP snapshot application, or cache rebuild, invalid enabled configs
produce a validation/construction warning and omit this instance from
the published plugin cache rather than rejecting the surrounding
snapshot. `ferrum-edge validate` can therefore exit 0 with optional
plugin warnings; inspect those warnings to confirm the alert instance
is active.

enabled.description: Master runtime switch for this plugin instance.

default_cooldown_seconds.description: Per-rule fallback cooldown. Cooldown is tracked per `(rule, proxy, channel)`.

default_min_request_count.description: Per-rule fallback for error-rate, latency-percentile, and grpc-status-rate rules.

default_resolved_window_seconds.description: Per-rule fallback recovery quiet period after a breach clears.

max_concurrent_dispatches.description: Maximum concurrent outbound notification requests. Excess alerts are dropped, not queued. Values above uint32 (`4294967295`) are rejected.

max_delivery_retries.description:
Number of re-attempts after the initial send for transient
transport/HTTP failures (408/429/5xx and connect/timeout errors).
Retries hold the dispatch semaphore permit and never enqueue extra
work. Permanent failures (other 4xx) are not retried.

delivery_retry_base_ms.description: Initial jittered backoff delay between transient delivery retries.

delivery_retry_max_ms.description:
Upper bound for exponential jittered backoff between transient
delivery retries. The constructor requires this to be
`>= delivery_retry_base_ms`. That sibling comparison is
constructor-only; this schema cannot assert it.

quiet_hours_utc.description: UTC time windows where Trigger alerts are suppressed. Resolve alerts still dispatch.

channels.description: Map of channel name to channel definition. Rule `channels` entries reference these names.

rules.description: Alert rules evaluated per matched proxy. At least one rule must be active.

ProxyAlertsDisabledDraftRule.description:
Explicitly disabled draft rule. Runtime skips these before validation,
so incomplete, unknown, or otherwise invalid fields are allowed when
`enabled` is the boolean `false`. Active complete rules must not use
this branch (`enabled: false` is excluded from active variants).

webhook_url.description: Discord-compatible webhook URL. Prefer `webhook_url_env` for secrets.

webhook_url_env.description: Environment variable containing the Discord webhook URL.

ProxyAlertsEmailAddress.description:
ASCII addr-spec as enforced by the constructor (no quoted local parts,
comments, or address literals; local-part dots cannot start, end, or
repeat). `format: email` is an annotation; this pattern is the
enforceable grammar. Constructor also caps the local part at 64 bytes.

ProxyAlertsEmailChannel.description:
Native SMTP delivery. TLS is mandatory: `starttls` upgrades the session
and fails closed when the relay does not advertise STARTTLS, and
`implicit_tls` handshakes immediately (SMTPS). Plaintext SMTP is not
offered, `AUTH` is never sent before the handshake completes, and
certificate verification is always enforced (this channel does not honor
`FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY`; use `FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH` for private CAs).
Username and password (inline or `*_env`) must be paired: either both
sides are set or neither is.

smtp_host.description: SMTP relay hostname or IP literal. No scheme, port, path, or credentials. Literal IPs must pass the resolved backend egress policy at admission (including allow/deny CIDRs and dangerous-range overrides). Construction does not resolve DNS; every send rechecks the resolved IP before connecting.

smtp_port.description: SMTP port. Defaults to 587 for `starttls` and 465 for `implicit_tls`.

tls_mode.description: TLS posture for the session. Both values complete a verified handshake before any credential or message data is written.

tls_server_name.description: Verified TLS identity override. Defaults to `smtp_host`.

username.description: SMTP AUTH username. Prefer `username_env`. Must be paired with `password` or `password_env`.

username_env.description: Environment variable containing the SMTP AUTH username.

password.description: SMTP AUTH password. Prefer `password_env`. Redacted from lower-privilege plugin projections and audit records; full-admin reads remain raw by repository policy. Must be paired with `username` or `username_env`.

password_env.description: Environment variable containing the SMTP AUTH password.

from.description: Envelope and header sender address (max 254 bytes, ASCII addr-spec).

subject_template.description:
Subject template. Schema `maxLength` is a character ceiling for
tooling. The constructor enforces a 1024-byte UTF-8 bound (a
600-character string of `é` is 1200 bytes and is rejected), rejects
empty strings, and rejects unbalanced `${` placeholders.

body_template.description:
Plain-text body template. Adds `${fields}`, the notification's
key/value rows rendered as `Name: value` lines. Schema `maxLength`
is a character ceiling; the constructor enforces a 65536-byte UTF-8
bound, rejects empty strings, and rejects unbalanced `${`
placeholders.

helo_name.description: EHLO identity. Defaults to the domain of `from`.

connect_timeout_ms.description: Applied independently to DNS resolution, TCP connect, and the TLS handshake, so a stalled connect can take up to three times this value before it fails.

command_timeout_ms.description: Bounds each SMTP command/reply exchange, including DATA.

ProxyAlertsEnvName.description:
Name of a `FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>` environment variable
(`<NAME>` uppercase `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*`) resolved at construction.
Any other process environment variable, including every other
`FERRUM_*` setting, is refused at admission with a 400. The named
variable must also be set and nonempty at construction; that
process-environment check is constructor-only.

classes.description: Error classes counted by this rule. HTTP rules also check `body_error_class`.

threshold_count.description: Alert when at least this many matching errors occur in the window.

threshold_percent.description: Alert when the matching status-code percentage is at least this value.

min_request_count.description: Minimum total requests in the window before the percentage can alert.

threshold_count.description:
Alert when at least this many completed gRPC transactions carry a
matching terminal application status in the window. Evaluated from
the terminal `log()` summary after buffered, trailers-only, and
streamed bodies finish. HTTP transport status is not consulted.

ProxyAlertsGrpcStatusList.description:
Terminal gRPC application statuses to match. Integers are standard codes
`0..=16`. The string `OTHER` matches malformed (`u32::MAX`) and future
out-of-range codes, matching the bounded StatsD/Prometheus bucket.
Distinct from HTTP `status_codes`.

threshold_percent.description:
Alert when the matching gRPC-status percentage among gRPC
transactions is at least this value. Plain HTTP samples do not
enter the denominator.

min_request_count.description: Minimum gRPC transactions in the window before the percentage can alert.

ProxyAlertsHttpUrl.description:
HTTP or HTTPS URL with a host and no `user:pass@` userinfo. Empty
strings are rejected. `format: uri` is a Draft 2020-12 annotation;
this pattern is the enforceable constructor approximation
(constructor also parses the URL and rejects a missing host).

metric.description: Latency metric to observe. `stream_duration_ms` applies to TCP/UDP/DTLS/WebSocket sessions and is measured on a process-monotonic clock (not UTC wall time); connect/disconnect timestamps remain civil-clock values for rendering. The other metrics apply to HTTP-family summaries.

threshold_ms.description: Alert when the bucket upper-bound estimate for the percentile is strictly greater than this threshold.

min_request_count.description: Minimum observations in the window before the percentile can alert.

from.description: UTC start time in strict HH:MM form.

to.description: UTC end time in strict HH:MM form. Values earlier than `from` wrap past midnight.

weekdays.description: Days the window applies to (`0 = Sunday` ... `6 = Saturday`). Omit or use `[]` for every day.

resolved_window_seconds.description: How long the rule must stay below threshold before a Resolve notification is sent.

ProxyAlertsRule.description:
Active rules are discriminator-selected closed variants. An explicit
`enabled: false` draft object is also accepted and may contain
incomplete or unknown fields; runtime skips drafts before validation.
Active variants reject `enabled: false` so a complete disabled rule
cannot satisfy more than one `oneOf` branch.

ProxyAlertsRuleCommon.description: Shared rule fields. Closed-object enforcement lives on each selected rule variant via `unevaluatedProperties: false` so common and type-specific keys compose correctly.

name.description: Unique rule name within this plugin config.

enabled.description: Active rules are enabled when this field is omitted or `true`. Use `ProxyAlertsDisabledDraftRule` (`enabled: false`) for incomplete drafts.

channels.description: Channel names from the top-level `channels` map.

webhook_url.description: Slack incoming webhook URL. Prefer `webhook_url_env` for secrets.

webhook_url_env.description: Environment variable containing the Slack incoming webhook URL.

threshold_count.description: Alert when at least this many matching responses occur in the window.

causes.description: Stream disconnect causes counted by this rule.

threshold_count.description: Alert when at least this many matching disconnects occur in the window.

webhook_url.description: Microsoft Teams incoming webhook URL. Prefer `webhook_url_env` for secrets.

webhook_url_env.description: Environment variable containing the Teams incoming webhook URL.

url.description: HTTP(S) endpoint URL. Prefer `url_env` for secrets.

url_env.description: Environment variable containing the HTTP(S) endpoint URL.

method.description:
HTTP method. Case-insensitive; the constructor normalizes to POST,
PUT, or PATCH. Spellings such as `post` and `pAtCh` are accepted.

headers.description: Headers sent with the webhook request. JSON content types JSON-escape template substitutions.

body_template.description:
Template body. Supports generic notification variables plus
proxy_alerts variables such as `${rule_name}`, `${proxy_name}`,
`${incident_key}` (stable per plugin config + namespace + proxy +
rule; use it as the receiver's correlation key, e.g. PagerDuty
`dedup_key`),
`${observed}`, `${threshold}`, `${sample_count}` (total samples in
the rule window), `${window_seconds}`, and `${reason}`. Empty
strings are allowed. Unbalanced `${`
placeholders are rejected at construction; JSON Schema cannot
express balanced-placeholder syntax.
